cards.text: When the day of Pentecost comes, Jesus' followers are all together in one place. ALL of them. Same room, same time. Friend, I once tried to line up six cookie cutters for one picture, and SOMEBODY always rolled off the counter.
So they're sitting there in the house. Quiet. Then, SUDDENLY, a sound comes from heaven and fills the WHOLE house.

cards.question: What is the sound from heaven like?
Along with that sound filling the house, what do Jesus' followers see?
The tongues like flames of fire separate and come to rest on each one of them.

cards.text: Then they are ALL filled with the Holy Spirit. Not most of them. Not just the front row. ALL of them.

cards.question: Filled with the Holy Spirit, what do Jesus' followers begin to do?

cards.text: Now, Jerusalem has God-fearing Jews living there from every nation under heaven. EVERY nation, friend. That's a whole lot of different ways to say "good morning."

cards.question: When the sound rings out, a crowd comes together in bewilderment, because each one hears Jesus' followers speaking his own ___.

cards.text: Astounded and amazed, the crowd asks, "Are not all these who are speaking Galileans?" I can hear it now. Wait. WAIT. Run that back.

cards.question: The crowd can't figure out how each of them is hearing these Galileans in his own native language.

cards.text: Then the crowd runs down where they're all from: Parthians, Medes, Elamites, folks from Mesopotamia to Egypt, visitors from Rome, Cretans and Arabs, both Jews and converts to Judaism. That is the BIGGEST "so where y'all from?" I have ever heard.

cards.question: Every one of them hears these Galileans declaring the ___ of God in their own tongues.
Once they hear Jesus' followers speaking, the whole crowd understands right away what it all means.

cards.text: But not everybody in that crowd is impressed. Some of them start mocking.

cards.question: What do the mockers in the crowd say about Jesus' followers?

answers.text: They are drunk on new wine

cards.text: So half the crowd is amazed, the other half is mocking, and nobody knows what to make of it. Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "so where y'all from?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card runs four sentences: the setup, 'ALL of them.', 'Same room, same time.' and the cookie cutter joke. It goes over the opening card's 3-sentence limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new event to his backstory in the Millers' kitchen: lining up the six cutters for a picture, with one 'always' rolling off the counter. Jokes can only make up small moments around his bakery. The line also clashes with the backstory, where he caught the cutters with his mustache when they wobbled near the edge. 'Once tried' and 'always rolled off' also contradict each other, so the joke fails the 'huh?' test.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The story card runs three sentences ('So they're sitting there in the house.' 'Quiet.' 'Then, SUDDENLY…'). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs four sentences ('Then they are ALL filled…' 'Not most of them.' 'Not just the front row.' 'ALL of them.'). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs three sentences ('Now, Jerusalem has…' 'EVERY nation, friend.' 'That's a whole lot…'). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card runs five sentences: the quote, 'I can hear it now.', 'Wait.', 'WAIT.' and 'Run that back.' Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank 'declaring the ___ of God' (wonders, laws or judgments) tests wording, not meaning. No earlier card sets up what the followers are declaring, so the baker can only guess the BSB word.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The story card is flat narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice ('But not everybody in that crowd is impressed. Some of them start mocking.'). It reads stripped down.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The last card recaps verses 12 to 13, which cards 14 to 16 already covered, before the 'story isn't over' line. Since verse 13 was asked on card 16, this card should be just the 'story isn't over' line.

'Half the crowd is amazed, the other half is mocking' adds a split the text never gives, since Acts 2:13 says only 'others.' 'Nobody knows what to make of it' is contradicted by the mockers in 2:13, who give their own explanation: 'They are drunk on new wine!'

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
